newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks post record after marginal rise.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks post record after marginal rise.

text.p: Swiss shares managed to post another record close on Thursday even though they slipped back from early gains to end near the day's lows.
Swiss indices were bolstered by clear gains in Novartis and to some extent Nestle, dealers said.
Prospects were described as good. "There seems to be a general upward trend in the market," one dealer noted.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 7.5 points, or 0.13 percent, at 5,669.9 after coming off an all-time high of 5,705.2. The day's low was at 5,663.8 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index was up 6.34 points, or 0.18 percent, to 3,577.89.
Bourse volume was a higher-than-average 2.67 billion francs.
Trade was described as nervous, but liquidity was still high. "It's better to move with the market and be prepared for a selling wave rather than just wait," one dealer said.
Novartis registered stock led the actives list, adding 29 francs to 2,367. The stock has drawn the market's attention since a research and development presentation one week ago.

Roche underperformed the market, gaining 15 francs to 13,505. Dealers said there may be some switching from Roche to Novartis. "There is a feeling that Novartis may be the new star in Swiss pharmaceutical shares," one trader noted.
Nestle edged up six francs to 1,943, still bolstered by low raw coffee prices and by technical factors,

Insurer Zurich added six francs to 589 after breaking a resistance level around 575/580. The stock has surged in the past few sessions on renewed rumours that the company was about to purchase U.S. asset manager Scudder.
Zurich has declined comment on the rumours, which have circulated on and off since late May.
Sulzer tumbled 43 francs to 1,270 after saying the issue price for shares in its Sulzer Medica unit being spun off was indicated at 300 to 350 francs per share.
Dealers said this was sharply lower than expected. One trader said Sulzer Medica shares had been changing hands in grey market trading at 500 francs and more.
Alusuisse was hit by profit taking after its recent rise, slipping 13 francs to 1,493.
